rules: Users, registered accounts, channels, viewers, subscribers, videos and views are different units.
A policy rate is not an income forecast and no rate has the same denominator by default.
Public API counts are not platform-wide population measures.
A user's demographic or political identity cannot be inferred from watched or published content.
Community labels may overlap and cannot be summed without deduplication.
Unobserved quantities remain null.
Use dated public evidence for policy claims and documented methods for population estimands.
Program eligibility, payment-account currency, creator residence, viewer country, and payment address are different concepts.
Virtual gifts pay creators through Rubies; Jewels are not equivalent to a gross-to-creator currency exchange.
Online Shopping and sponsor discovery are routes to commerce rather than fixed creator payments.
Registered thumbnail impressions, Shorts feed presentations and video starts are separate countable events.
A casual or regular viewer is a lookback-window classification, not a purchasing tier.
An archived live replay and its original live broadcast can share viewers and should not have their estimated audiences summed without deduplication.
Copyright claims, legal removal requests, and copyright strikes are different enforcement units.
Music revenue-sharing adjustments, license cash expenses, and disputed-payment holds cannot be double-counted.
A Google Account, YouTube publishing channel, verified feature level and approved monetized channel are separate objects.
Advanced features may be reached through channel history; optional ID/video verification is not a requirement for every channel.
Uploading a file and publicly publishing a video are distinct events.
Syndicated copies of a creator survey count as one independent sample, not independent replication.
Mixed-platform income thresholds do not identify YouTube-only earnings or a newcomer cohort.
The intended newcomer earning population must retain zero earners and define time, costs and sampling frame.
A TV-set viewing series is a subset of all in-home connected-device viewing; do not add them.
Country/age prevalence and multi-market online respondent averages are not interchangeable with global people counts.
Multi-language audio tracks attached to one video do not create independent video objects or distinct viewer populations.
Selected non-primary-language watch-time share is neither observed causal uplift nor equivalent to foreign-country user reach.
August 24, 2026 changed public viewCount to first-frame playback starts, creating a public view series comparability break.
Engaged attention, qualified YPP views, qualified public watch hours, ad impressions and individual playback starts retain separate units.
